newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Distral SA unveils German deal.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Distral SA unveils German deal.

text.p: One of Colombia's largest machine-tool and equipment manufacturers Distral SA said Monday it was selling an 18 percent stake in the company to German industrial group Deutsche Babcock.
The deal comes after two years of behind-the-scenes negotiations and will mark the start of the German group's expansion into Latin America, a Distral spokesman said.
Distral said it will issue $24.5 million in new shares in the primary market by February 1997, $11.5 million of which will be sold to Deutsche Babcock.

The company spokesman, who did not wish to be named, said the German group, made up of 170 individual companies with investments in the United States and Asia, may eventually take on a 50 percent stake in Distral.
"Deutsche Babcock has decided it wants to attack the Latin American market and has opted to set up a base in Colombia," the Distral spokesman said.

Distral, in which U.S. firm Lancaster Steel Co has a 38 percent holding, had assets of 172.4 billion pesos as of September this year and reported net profits of 1.12 billion pesos in the first nine months of 1996.

Distral is currently working on a $750 million contract to refit the Termobarranquilla power plant in the Caribbean coastal port of Barranquilla and is fitting out pumping stations along the 500 mile (800 km) Ocensa SA pipeline, which once constructed will transport oil from Colombia's oil-rich eastern plains to the terminal at Covenas on the Caribbean coast.

Distral SA is rarely traded on Colombia's stock exchanges but rumors of the Deutsche Babcock deal drove share prices up to 40 pesos each in Medellin and 34 pesos each in Bogota at close of trade Friday.
